transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
With more congressional race calls today, the Democrats will claim 243 seats with at
least 152 in Republican hands come January.
So far, Democrats have flipped 37 seats and Republicans have flipped one in Texas.
32 was redrawn as part of the GOP's nationwide redistricting push.
At last check, there were still 35 races yet to be called.
Democrats lead in 13 of them.
Republicans lead in 21.
Another in Louisiana is heading to a runoff in December.
Now the blue wave is driven by voter's fury about the cost of fuel.
NPR's Willa Rubin sources say, "Don't hold your breath for lower gasoline and diesel
prices."
Oil is dictated by a complex global market.
Congress has limited powers to change that.
But they can make escalation more costly.
They can pass resolutions, attach conditions to war spending, and hold back confirmations
of key officials.
They can also push the president to end the war in Iran.
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer told reporters on Wednesday that Democrats are intent
on ending the war.
The president has veto power, and the president can escalate the war or end it.
Even when the war ends, Brent crude prices could drop pretty quickly, but it would take
longer for lower gasoline and diesel.
The whole oil supply chain would have to recover.
That could take months, maybe three to six, and that's assuming all goes well.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
Voters across Ohio have sent a clear message.
They don't want AI data centers in their communities.
And PR's Andrea Hsu reports the issue was on local ballots across the state.
Ohio had by far the most ballot initiatives of any state focused on data centers.
Voters in a dozen and a half communities approved 21 measures that will either keep data centers
out altogether or introduce hurdles to their development.
Attorney Nick Owens is with the grassroots group Conserve Ohio, which backed a number
of the measures.
It's clear when Ohioans are given the choice whether to approve or reject hyperscale data
center developments, they overwhelmingly reject them.
Ohio's governor-elect Amy Acton has called for a conditional moratorium on new data centers
to ensure they cover their utility costs, meet environmental standards, and are built
with union labor.
Andrea Hsu, NPR News.
Students workers pensioners returning to the streets of Lyon, France today heard here through
Reuters with demands for higher pay and more school funding.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley says people have been staging these mass protests for more than
a month.
It's becoming very tense, the situation in France.
We're six months ahead of a presidential election.
It's not clear who these protests are benefiting.
The far left comes out and capitalizes on them.
That's NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reporting.
You're listening to NPR News.
L.A. City Council member Nithya Rahman has won the L.A.'s mayor race, ousting incumbent
mayor Karen Bass, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
Rahman, a DSA affiliated candidate who angered the Democratic Socialists of L.A. in her role
on the council, will be the third mayor with ties to the progressive left following New
York's Zaraan Mamdani and D.C. mayor-elect Janice Lewis George.
Well, Washington, D.C. has just joined a small but growing number of major U.S. cities to
elect Democratic Socialists as mayor, but D.C. is subject to strict federal oversight.
So as NPR's Michaela Gray tells us, the next mayor of the nation's capital will have to
work with President Trump to enact her priorities.
Mayor-elect Janice Lewis George says she'll begin her term by initiating a conversation
with President Trump about affordable housing.
We're going in there with some proposals that we hope the president will be excited about
because I know he has an interest in building more housing.
Tateesh Natara, professor of political science at the University of Massachusetts, says Trump
could be willing to work with her.
And I think he wants to put his stamp on the city, and one of the ways he can do that is
through housing.
And that'd be similar to New York City mayor's Zaraan Mamdani's approach.
Michaela Gray, NPR News, Washington.
Police are investigating a shooting in Des Moines, Iowa, in which a post office worker
allegedly shot two of her co-workers and injured a third.
Here's Sergeant Paul Perisic.
Fortunately, we were able to get here quickly and make sure that we stop the killing before
it got any worse.
He says the suspect was taken into custody.
The Dow is down more than 1,600 points.
You're listening to NPR News.

Lyon, France students, workers and pensioners march for higher pay and more school funding
